question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "25-year-old woman with forearm pain" -> "history of ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation" -> "tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle" -> "marked weakness in extending right middle finger" -> "radial deviation on wrist extension" -> "indicates possible radial nerve involvement" -> "posterior interosseous nerve is a branch of the radial nerve" -> "likely affected due to history and symptoms" -> 85%

enhanced_information: The patient presents with pain and weakness in the right forearm and hand, with a history of ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation. Physical examination reveals tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle, marked weakness in extending the right middle finger, and radial deviation during wrist extension. These symptoms suggest dysfunction of the radial nerve, specifically the posterior interosseous nerve, which innervates the wrist extensors and is responsible for finger extension. The history of trauma and the specific weakness pattern strongly indicate that the posterior interosseous nerve is the most likely affected nerve in this case.
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history suggest a specific nerve injury. The marked weakness in extending the right middle finger indicates a problem with the extensor muscles, which are primarily innervated by the radial nerve. The tenderness located distal to the lateral epicondyle aligns with the area where the posterior interosseous nerve branches off the radial nerve. The radial deviation during wrist extension further supports the idea of a radial nerve issue, as this occurs when the wrist extensors are compromised. Given the history of trauma (ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation), it is plausible that the posterior interosseous nerve was affected, leading to the observed symptoms. Therefore, the most likely affected nerve in this case is the posterior interosseous nerve, which is a branch of the radial nerve responsible for innervating the extensor muscles of the forearm.
